text:
Step 1 – nitration of toluene  
Mixed-acid nitration of toluene gives mainly the para product.  For the rest of the sequence it is simplest (and common in problem sets) to take 1 as p-nitrotoluene.

Step 2 – oxidation with MnO₂ / H₂SO₄  
Under these conditions a benzylic methyl group is oxidised to an aldehyde; 1 is converted to p-nitrobenzaldehyde 2.

Step 3 – reaction of 2 with acetone / aq. NaOH  
Base removes an α-hydrogen from acetone to give its enolate, which undergoes a single crossed-aldol condensation with the aldehyde, followed by dehydration:

p-NO₂–C₆H₄–CHO  +  CH₃COCH₃   →   p-NO₂–C₆H₄–CH=CH–COCH₃   (3)

Only one benzaldehyde unit reacts (no excess is specified), so the product is the monobenzalacetone (a p-nitro-chalcone).

Structure and symmetry of 3  
• All atoms can lie in one plane; that plane is a mirror plane σ.  
• Because the two ends of the molecule are different (p-nitrophenyl on one side, a methyl group on the other) there is no C₂ (or higher) rotational axis and no inversion centre.

Thus the only non-trivial symmetry element is a single mirror plane: the point group is Cₛ.

(A) C₂h – requires both C₂ and i   (absent)  
(B) C₃ – requires a 3-fold axis   (absent)  
(C) D₂h – requires three C₂ axes and i (absent)  
(D) Cₛ – one mirror plane only   (present)

Answer: D
